pageCache.text:
Making
my way.
The Independent Prep School for Girls aged 2 to 11 years in Buckinghamshire.
Welcome to Maltman’s Green School: where girls have been making their way since 1918
At Maltman’s Green, we have a proud legacy of over 100 years of pushing the boundaries of girls’ education. Our commitment to nurturing girls begins from age 2, with flexible childcare options designed to support busy families. We provide a nurturing environment, where every pupil is encouraged to face challenges and take risks, developing resilience and confidence, that will serve them well throughout their lives.
We are celebrating an exceptional set of 11+ examination results this year, with an outstanding pass rate that reflects both the dedication of pupils and the exceptional support and exam preparation offered at our private school. 78% of pupils who took the exam, passed the Buckinghamshire 11+, more than double the county average. In addition, our Year girls achieved an incredible 17 scholarship offers, recognising their academic, sporting and creative talents.
As a parent, you want the best for your child, and we share that commitment.
Maltman’s Green is among the trusted private schools in Buckinghamshire, recognised by the Good Schools Guide for the quality of education and pastoral care we provide.
Our dedicated educators work closely with families to ensure each girl feels valued and supported. Our curriculum is designed to cater to your daughter’s unique strengths and interests, empowering her to thrive in all subjects.
The freedom of an all girls education sees our girls consistently achieve exceptional 11+ results, demonstrating the confidence and academic excellence needed to succeed.
She’s an amplified version of herself.
At our independent girls’ school in Buckinghamshire, we recognise that education extends beyond academics. We are committed to developing well-rounded girls equipped with the skills and values necessary. to navigate the world around them. Our fabulous facilities and extensive range of extracurricular offerings—from sports and the performing arts to languages and public speaking—ensures that your daughter can explore her interests and find her passions.
Join us on this journey of discovery and growth. Together, we are making your daughter’s future brighter at Maltman’s Green School.

pageCache.pageTitle: Languages at Maltman's Green | Inspiring Multilingual Learning
pageCache.text:
Making my words travel the world.
Everyday we make the world bigger and brighter by giving our girls the tools to communicate across cultures.
Starting from Little Malties at age 2, our girls are introduced to French, taught by our talented teaching team of native French speakers. As they progress through the school, they are immersed in engaging lessons designed to spark their curiosity and enthusiasm for languages. By the time they reach Year 6, they have the opportunity to expand their linguistic repertoire by learning Spanish, further enhancing their communication skills and cultural understanding.
Our approach to language learning isn’t just about vocabulary and grammar – it’s about making their confidence grow by engaging them in fun, interactive activities that bring language to life. Whether through songs, stories, role-playing or cultural celebrations, we ensure that every girl is excited to use her new language skills, both inside and outside the classroom.
Through our comprehensive languages programme, we foster a love of language learning and cultural exploration from an early age, helping each girl to broaden her horizons, develop new skills and build the confidence to express herself in multiple languages.
In today’s globalised world, understanding different cultures is more important than ever. This a core part of our language teaching. Our girls don’t just learn how to speak another language; they gain insights into the cultures, customs and traditions of French and Spanish speaking countries. This cultural immersion helps our girls develop a broader perspective, fostering open-mindedness and respect for other cultures.
By giving our girls the ability to speak and understand other languages, we are equipping them with a skill that will open doors throughout their lives. Whether they use these skills in future education, careers or travel, the language foundation they build here will serve them well in a globalised world.
Join us in making their future more connected. Through our language programme, we are preparing each girl to be a confident global citizen, ready to navigate an international landscape with ease and grace.

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts at Maltman's - Drama, Music & Dance Facilities
pageCache.text:
Making the spotlight ours.
At Maltman’s Green, we believe the Performing Arts are an essential part of every girl’s education.
Through drama, music, and dance, our pupils develop confidence, creativity, and self-expression, while learning valuable life skills such as teamwork, communication and leadership. From their earliest years, our girls are encouraged to explore their creative potential, with numerous opportunities to take to the stage and showcase their talents.
Our state-of-the-art facilities include a purpose-built performing arts centre, with a performance space, tiered theatre seating, audio visual facilities, and a dance studio, providing the perfect environment for our girls to immerse themselves in the world of performing arts.
Whether it’s through weekly drama lessons, LAMDA, music ensembles, or dance classes, every girl is encouraged to find her voice and discover her passion.
Music is at the heart of our school, with a rich programme of individual and group lessons led by specialist teachers. Girls can choose from a wide range of instruments and are invited to join one of our many musical ensembles, including choirs, orchestras and bands. Regular performances, both within the school and in the wider community, give our girls the chance to shine in front of an audience and further develop their confidence.
Our drama productions are a highlight of the school calendar, with girls throughout the school participating in exciting and imaginative performances. From large-scale productions to class plays, these events allow our pupils to develop their acting skills and experience the thrill of performing in front of an audience. Whether they dream of becoming a West End star or simply enjoy the fun and camaraderie of being on stage, there is something for everyone.
Dance is another vibrant aspect of life at Maltman’s. With a dedicated dance studio and a variety of classes, including ballet, street, musical theatre and contemporary, our girls have every opportunity to express themselves through movement.

pageCache.pageTitle: Making Our Voices Heard With Our Own Maltman's Green Voice Award
pageCache.text:
Making Our Voices Heard.
Finding one’s voice is an essential part of personal growth, and we are proud to introduce Maltman’s Green’s very own Your Voice Award.
This unique programme is designed to help our girls discover, develop and express their voices with clarity, confidence and conviction. The Your Voice Award aims to empower every girl in our Prep School to articulate her thoughts eloquently, building essential communication skills that will serve her throughout her life.
The Your Voice Award covers a range of verbal communication skills, including oracy, recitation, prosody, rendition and debate. Through this award, our girls refine their public speaking abilities and cultivate critical thinking, persuasive techniques and self-expression. These essential skills are integrated into subjects such as English, Drama, History and Current Affairs, ensuring that the Your Voice Award becomes a core part of the curriculum.
By learning to express themselves in a variety of formats, our girls will build the confidence to speak in any setting, from the classroom to formal presentations. The award also encourages them to think critically about the world around them, nurturing informed, thoughtful young minds who are prepared to engage in meaningful discussions.
The Your Voice Award isn’t just about speaking – it’s about building self-assurance, teamwork and leadership. Each girl has the opportunity to engage in group debates and solo presentations, creating a supportive environment where they can challenge themselves and each other. Our girls grow into articulate, confident individuals ready to take on the challenges of tomorrow.
As they progress through the programme, they will be encouraged to use their voices to make a difference in their school, community and beyond.
Discover how the Your Voice Award is making the communication skills of our girls strong, their confidence soar and their futures bright.
Visit us to find our more about the power of self-expression and watch your daughter find her voice.

pageCache.pageTitle: Benefits Of A Balanced Approach To Learning | Maltman's Green
pageCache.text:
Tuesday 1 April 2025
From STEAM to the Arts: Why a Balanced Curriculum is Key for Your Daughter’s Success
At Maltman’s Green School, we believe that a balanced curriculum—which includes STEAM education (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Mathematics)—is essential for nurturing creativity, critical thinking, and academic success in girls. This integrated approach prepares them for a rapidly changing world, equipping them with the necessary life skills to thrive.
What is a STEAM Education?
A STEAM education combines science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics into one comprehensive learning model. This holistic approach helps students think more critically, creatively, and broadly, preparing them for real-world applications to encourage intellectual, emotional, and physical growth.
By blending STEAM with the arts, we provide a well-rounded educational experience that supports academic achievement while fostering personal development, nurturing our girls to help them succeed in any field.
STEAM vs STEM Education: What’s the Difference and why is it important?
While traditional STEM education focuses on science, technology, engineering, and mathematics, our STEAM programme integrates the arts. This encourages students to explore and understand the interconnectedness of various disciplines, to broaden their perspective and promote creative problem-solving inside the classroom and in everyday life.
STEAM in Early Childhood Education
Introducing STEAM in early childhood education sparks curiosity and builds foundational skills that students carry with them throughout their academic careers.
At Maltman’s Green, we begin STEAM activities at a young age, priming students for success both intellectually and emotionally.
This early exposure nurtures both their analytical thinking and their emotional expression, ensuring they grow up to be confident, curious learners who are ready to tackle complex challenges inside and outside the classroom – preparing her for lifelong success, regardless of whether she chooses a career in science or the arts.
Encouraging A Passion for Lifelong Learning
As parents, it’s important to support your daughter’s exploration in both areas. Encourage her to participate in STEAM clubs, coding workshops or science fairs while also engaging in art classes, drama or music.
This dual exposure can ignite a passion for learning that transcends traditional boundaries. Through this exposure, students are more motivated and excited to pursue diverse academic interests, fostering a love for learning that lasts well beyond school.
Preparing Her for Success: Life Beyond Maltman’s Green
At Maltman’s Green School, we prioritise a balanced curriculum that nurtures both the analytical and creative sides of our pupils. By fostering diverse interests through a wide variety of intra and extracurricular activities, we help girls develop into well-rounded individuals ready to take on future challenges.
As a leading independent school in Buckinghamshire, we at Maltman’s Green are committed to preparing students for life, from Early Years through to Pre-Prep, Prep through to the 11 plus exams and beyond.
Our top-class facilities, including Olympic-sized swimming pool, state-of-the-art science labs, and extensive outdoor learning spaces, support the development of both intellectual and physical well-being, ensuring students have everything they need to thrive.
By fostering diverse interests, we help our girls become confident, well-rounded individuals prepared for the challenges of tomorrow. This commitment is reflected in the 13 senior school scholarships awarded in 2025, together with an 70% pass rate in 11 plus – showing how we prioritise both intellectual development and personal growth while ensuring students have the support they need to succeed.
If you’re keen to discover more about how Maltman’s Green School champions a balanced curriculum for your daughter’s success, request a prospectus today and book an open day visit today at our independent girl’s school in Gerrards Cross, Buckinghamshire.

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra-Curricular Activities at Maltman's Green - Arts to Sport
pageCache.text:
Making time for what we love.
Superb extra curricular provision
With over 120 clubs on offer from Reception onwards, our extra-curricular is extra special.
Click to find out more…
An average of 4 sporting fixtures every week.
From vibrant music groups, orchestras, and choirs to a variety of dance forms including contemporary, ballet and street dance, girls are encouraged to explore their artistic talents. Drama is also very popular, with performances supported by LAMDA qualifications, which enhance the acting abilities of our girls and build confidence in public speaking.
A diverse sports program caters to a wide range of interests and abilities. From traditional team sports like netball, football and cricket to individual pursuits such as gymnastics, fencing and athletics, there is something for every girl to enjoy.
Finding one’s voice is an essential part of personal growth, and we are proud to offer the Your Voice Award. This unique programme is designed to help our girls discover, develop, and express their voices with clarity, confidence, and conviction. Through the Your Voice Award, we empower every girl in our Prep School to articulate her thoughts eloquently, nurturing communication skills that will serve her throughout life. By fostering self-expression and public speaking abilities, we ensure our pupils are equipped to engage meaningfully in any setting, whether in the classroom, during debates, or future professional endeavors.

With engaging lessons, interactive activities and practical conversation practice, our girls develop proficiency in the language and an appreciation for the rich cultural contexts behind them. Whether preparing for future travel, future international studies or simply exploring new languages ready for secondary school, our clubs inspire curiosity and confidence in language learning.
Our extensive extra-curricular programme allows each girl to discover and develop her unique interests, fostering a sense of achievement, teamwork and collaboration. Every girl is given the platform to shine.

Every one of our activities helps to instil the confidence and self-belief our pupils need to thrive in the pool, on the stage, in the classroom and beyond.
We also understand that every girl is unique, which is why our programme is designed to offer breadth and flexibility. Making their choice as broad as possible means that your daughter will always find something she loves, whether it’s honing a new skill, pursuing a personal passion or just trying something different.

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra-Curricular Sports at Maltman's Green - Developing Skills
pageCache.text:
Making my spirit
lift our team.
Sport at Maltman’s is both enjoyable and empowering. Our comprehensive sports programme is designed to nurture each girl’s athletic abilities, promote teamwork and instil a passion for physical activity.
From a young age, our girls are introduced to a wide variety of sports, ensuring they have the opportunity to discover their passions and strengths. Our expertly designed curriculum includes everything from traditional team sports like netball and cricket to individual disciplines such as swimming and gymnastics. By offering diverse sporting experiences, we make sure that every girl can find her niche and thrive.
Sports is about more than just physical prowess; we foster a strong sense of teamwork and sportsmanship. Our girls participate in regular inter-house and inter-school matches and competitions, which not only challenge them to improve their skills but also teach them the importance of working together towards a common goal. Through these experiences, they learn valuable lessons in cooperation, leadership and resilience.
Through sport, our girls develop their physical skills and build confidence, resilience and a sense of camaraderie and team spirit.
Physical fitness is integral to overall wellbeing and we make it a priority. Our 12 acre site with extensive sports facilities, including our state-of-the-art 25m, 6 lane swimming pool, netball and tennis courts and outdoor playing fields and fully equipped gymnasium, provide the perfect environment for our girls to stay active and healthy. Our dedicated sports staff are committed to supporting each girl’s development, whether they are training for a competition or simply enjoying a game with friends.
We take pride in celebrating the achievements of all our girls, recognising their hard work and dedication both on and off the field. From awarding certificates for sporting excellence to showcasing their accomplishments in our weekly celebration assemblies and newsletters, we ensure that every girl’s efforts are acknowledged and celebrated.
Visit us and see how we provide a dynamic and supportive environment where every girl can excel in sport and enjoy the many benefits it brings.

pageCache.pageTitle: Charity & Community Work at Maltman's Green - Making an Impact
pageCache.text:
Making a difference.
We are committed to instilling in our pupils a deep understanding of a wide range of charitable needs, encouraging them to engage with international and national causes, the environment, their local communities and charities promoting children’s welfare.
Through their House system, they actively participate in pupil lead fundraising initiatives for charities whom they suggest and vote for, fostering a strong sense of responsibility and compassion.
Our community outreach extends beyond just fundraising with regular visits to local care homes to perform Christmas carols and music concerts throughout the year. Additionally, our pupils deliver Christmas gifts to neighbours, spreading that extra little bit of seasonal kindness and goodwill.
To recognise their charitable efforts, pupils are celebrated in our weekly Purple Print newsletter, highlighting their contributions to local and global communities.
From the youngest pupils to those preparing to leave, our girls are encouraged to take action, make a difference, and be a force for good in the world. By involving them in a range of charitable initiatives, we are making sure they understand the importance of giving back, not just within the school but in the wider community.
We believe in making charity a central part of every girl’s education.
Our charitable focus covers a variety of important areas, including support for international projects, environmental campaigns and charities that promote children’s welfare, both locally and globally. Whether they are raising funds for a featured charity, volunteering their time, or learning about the broader impact of their actions, we are making their awareness and compassion grow.
Making a difference through charity is also about personal development. As they engage with these initiatives, the girls learn valuable life skills such as teamwork, leadership and empathy. By supporting others, they build a stronger sense of community and understand that they have the power to make meaningful changes in the world.
Choosing Maltman’s Green means choosing a school where charity and community engagement are not just values, but everyday practices.

pageCache.pageTitle: Enrichment Programme at Maltman's Green - Life Beyond School
pageCache.text:
Making sure we are ready for our future
The Year 6 Enrichment Programme is designed to create lasting memories and teach valuable life skills while preparing our pupils for life beyond school.
Their final year is packed with a raft of activities that help them build real-world practical skills, such as a First Aid course, Young Enterprise project and Bikeability training.
They also enjoy immersive experiences such as a WW2 theme day, drama production and a “Build an App” day. Leadership skills are encouraged through Sports Leaders training and the Wise Up Team Building Day.
To cap off the year, fun events such as the Parent and Daughter Rounders match and picnic and a disco provide extra opportunities to make unforgettable memories that will last them a lifetime.
We believe in making their final year extraordinary. The Year 6 Enrichment Programme is not just about fun and games; it’s about making their transition to senior school seamless, preparing them with the skills and confidence they need for the next chapter of their journey.
By choosing Maltman’s Green, you’re ensuring that your daughter is not only academically prepared but is also emotionally and socially ready to thrive.
Our enrichment activities are carefully designed to make learning come to life. From building an app to leading their peers on the sports field, these experiences offer our girls the opportunities to develop practical knowledge, teamwork and leadership skills in a supportive environment.
What sets us apart is the balance between serious skill-building and joyful, memorable moments. Making their final year enjoyable is just as important as preparing the girls for what’s next.
Our Year 6 Enrichment Programme ensures they leave us with cherished memories, valuable skills, and the self-belief that will set them up for success.
Let us help make their future one filled with confidence, achievement, and lasting friendships.
Register your daughter today and give her the Maltman’s Green experience.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Trips and Residentials at Maltman's Green School
pageCache.text:
Making discoveries
beyond the classroom.
Trips are an integral part of our curriculum, with each year group enjoying excursions that align with the topics studied during the term.
From the very first trip, each excursion is designed to foster independence and curiosity, making their learning come to life through practical experiences. Whether they are visiting local historical sites, exploring museums or venturing into nature, our girls gain a deeper understanding of the world around them, all while building new friendships and creating memories.
Our trips and residentials programme makes their education an unforgettable journey, preparing them for a bright and adventurous future.
In addition to day trips, residential stays begin in Year 3 with an exciting one-night adventure at Longridge. Each year, the length of the residential trip increases, culminating in a four-night stay in France in Year 6. These experiences provide invaluable opportunities for learning, personal growth, bonding outside of the classroom and putting the ‘Maltman’s Mindsets’ into practise.
Making their experiences outside the classroom as rich as those inside is key to shaping well-rounded, confident individuals. Our residentials allow the girls to explore new environments, challenge themselves, and discover hidden talents.
By the time they reach Year 6, their four-night adventure in France is not only a highlight of their time at Maltman’s Green but also a testament to the personal growth they’ve experienced over the years.

Senior Leadership Team
Position: Headmistress
Qualifications: BA (Hons), PGCE
Mrs Morjaria joined Maltman’s Green in April 2026, bringing with her a wealth of senior leadership experience and a deep commitment to girls’ education.
Previously Deputy Head of Junior School (Academic) at Northwood College for Girls, Mrs Morjaria brings over 15 years’ experience in spearheading curriculum reform, driving whole school improvement and embedding coaching cultures that create lasting, meaningful impact. Most recently, she has worked as a Trust Consultant across 26 schools, fostering collaboration, leading senior leadership conferences and driving excellence at scale. As a member of the North London Schools Consortium 11+ Working Party, Ashmi brings to Maltman’s an invaluable understanding of the evolving expectations around senior school admissions and the qualities that leading independent schools look for in applicants.
Mrs Morjaria is passionate about inspiring Maltman’s girls to be confident, speak up and make their mark as change makers.
Read the Head’s Welcome here.
Mr Paramour has held senior leadership positions at a range of schools in both the independent and maintained sectors. He joined Maltman’s Green in September 2025 from Bancroft’s Prep School in North-East London. He is a published author, having co-authored two titles for Bloomsbury Education: The Grammar Book and The Writing Book. He has an undergraduate degree in Philosophy and a Masters degree in Medieval History. He takes a pragmatic, evidence-informed approach to teaching and learning and he is passionate about developing the girls’ critical thinking and debating skills. As well as writing and history, Mr Paramour’s interests include football, walking, baking, canoeing and travelling.
Mrs Gaynor was Head of Early Years here before becoming Deputy Head in September 2019. She successfully launched our Little Malties day care facility and has driven an individualised approach to learning in the Early Years where every child works at their own pace and is stretched and challenged within a safe and nurturing environment. Mrs Gaynor continues to implement initiatives that give these very youngest of our girls the best possible start to their early education. Mrs Gaynor has a PGCE and hands-on experience teaching KS2, Nursery and Reception. Before joining Maltman’s Green, she held the post of Head of Early Years at Northwood College.
Mrs Stevens graduated with a Bsc Social Research degree from London Metropolitan University and worked as an assistant auditor for the National Audit Office. She moved into local government and focused on the business development of the early education and childcare sectors within the boroughs of Kensington & Chelsea, Hammersmith & Fulham and Westminster. She moved into school business management in 2019, working for the Danes Educational Trust, before taking up the position of Bursar at Lockers Park, a boys Prep and Boarding School in Hertfordshire. Mrs Stevens is married with one teenage daughter and in her spare time, enjoys rambling and is an avid movie and theatre goer.
Ms Button’s teaching career spans 17 years and covers Early Years to KS2. Prior to starting at Maltman’s Green in December 2020 she was Head of Pre-Prep and educational consultant at Wellington College International, Shanghai, for over five years, and before that was an assistant head and head of Early Years in her home city of Leicester. Ms Button defines education as the key that unlocks doors and enjoys working closely with parents to ensure the educational journey is both positive and successful. With a degree in design and a Masters in history, Ms Button is a keen advocate of the Arts and this extends to her life beyond school, where she takes every opportunity to be creative. She is also a keen traveller and enjoys visiting new destinations.
Elizabeth Ullstein holds a BSc in Geography from Brunel University and a Master’s in Education from Durham University. She has spent most of her career teaching in the independent sector, bringing energy, expertise and a passion for inspiring pupils. A talented sportswoman, Mrs Ulstein represented England in lacrosse and enjoys playing cricket in her spare time. Her adventurous spirit has taken her to the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro, and she also holds a pilot’s licence. Whether in the classroom, on the sports field or exploring new horizons, Mrs Ulstein encourages pupils to embrace challenge and pursue their passions with confidence.

pageCache.pageTitle: How Nutrition Supports Learning at Maltman’s Green School
pageCache.text:
Thursday 22 May 2025
The Importance of Nutrition in Supporting Academic Success: How to Fuel Your Daughter’s Learning
Nutrition plays a crucial role in supporting your daughter’s academic success. At Maltman’s Green School, we understand that a well-balanced diet fuels not only physical health but also cognitive development. Discover more on how we promote a healthy balanced diet. Here are some tips for promoting healthy eating habits that will benefit her learning.
Start by involving your daughter in meal planning and preparation. Encourage her to choose healthy ingredients and participate in cooking. This involvement means she is able to practically learn what goes into meals. While doing this, teach the nutritional value of different foods and how they impact her energy and focus throughout the day.
Encourage a balanced diet that includes a variety of fruits, vegetables, whole grains and proteins. These nutrient-rich foods provide essential vitamins and minerals that support brain function and overall wellbeing.
Ensure she stays hydrated by drinking plenty of water throughout the day, as dehydration can negatively affect concentration and performance.
Additionally, establish regular mealtimes and encourage healthy snacks. Avoid sugary treats and processed foods, which can lead to energy crashes and hinder academic performance. Instead, offer nutritious snacks like fruits or yogurt to sustain her energy levels during study sessions.
Discuss the importance of breakfast as a crucial meal that sets the tone for the day. A healthy breakfast can enhance focus and cognitive function, improving her ability to learn and retain information.
At Maltman’s Green, we prioritise healthy eating habits and nutrition education, ensuring our girls are equipped with the knowledge and skills to make healthy choices. Our skilled catering team prepares authentic, delicious food using freshly sourced, seasonal, local ingredients, ensuring that every meal is both nutritious and flavourful. If you’d like to learn more about our approach to nutrition and its impact on academic success, book a tour of our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Rich History of Maltman's Green - Adaptations on Tradition
pageCache.text:
History
in the making.
Maltmans Green School has a century-long tradition of innovation, development and adaptation in education
Founded by Miss Chambers in 1918, her progressive and transformative principles were pioneering at the time – ‘…developing character and intellect while encouraging self-expression, self-belief, self-worth and compassion.’ —values that still endure today.
As a true trailblazer, Miss Chambers paved the way for women in the last century, and by following her example, we continue to shape a bright future for our pupils in the twenty-first century, ensuring they are fully prepared for the world ahead of them.
Today, Mrs. Morjaria, our current Headmistress, carries forward this proud legacy. Under her leadership, Maltman’s Green continues to blend tradition with forward-thinking, creating a nurturing environment where every girl is encouraged to reach her full potential. Mrs. Morjaria is passionate about maintaining the school’s core values of independence, creativity and initiative, while embracing modern educational practices to ensure that our pupils are fully prepared for the world of tomorrow.
While the school’s foundation was built by pioneers like Miss Chambers, it is Mrs. Morjaria’s commitment to excellence that drives our approach today. She ensures that the innovative spirit that defined our past remains central to how we educate and inspire our girls. By blending the best of both traditional values and contemporary learning, Maltman’s Green provides an environment where girls are empowered to become confident, capable and compassionate young women.
Choosing Maltman’s Green means choosing a school with a rich history and a bright future.
Under Mrs. Morjaria’s guidance, love and leadership we continue to honour our century-long tradition of preparing girls to make their way—ready to embrace the challenges and opportunities of the twenty-first century.

Why Outdoor Play is Important for Your Daughter’s Growth: Fun Activities to Try This Weekend
Outdoor exploration is more than just a chance for your daughter to run around, it plays a vital role in her development. For girls aged 2-11, spending time outside boosts physical, emotional, and cognitive growth. Here’s why outdoor activities matter and some fun ideas you can try with your daughter this weekend.
How Does Outdoor Play Affect a Child’s Development?
Physical Development Outdoor activities like climbing, running and balancing help girls build their motor skills and improve coordination. These physical challenges boost both strength and confidence. At Maltman’s Green, we prioritise outdoor learning and play as part of our curriculum, helping girls develop in a fun and natural way. Our outdoor space has two climbing frames, The Titan and Mini Titan, both of these offer fun, physical challenges for the girls.
Cognitive Development Nature provides endless opportunities for discovery. Encourage your daughter to explore her surroundings, whether it’s collecting leaves, identifying different plants or building a den. All of these activities will help her develop problem-solving skills and spark creativity. At Maltman’s Green, our private woodland provides an expansive and enriching environment for outdoor learning.
Building Confidence and Resilience Facing new outdoor challenges, like climbing a tree or navigating an obstacle course, teaches your daughter to push her limits and overcome her fears. These experiences build resilience, an essential skill that helps her face challenges both inside and outside the classroom.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Environmental Consciousness at Maltman's Green School
pageCache.text:
Making my school
a force for change.
We’re proud to be an Eco-School, holding prestigious Green Flag status in recognition of our commitment to sustainability.
Environmental consciousness is deeply embedded in our curriculum across all year groups, ensuring every pupil learns the importance of sustainable living. Our pupil lead Eco Council, composed of elected representatives from each year group, leads initiatives such as ‘Walk to School Week’, ‘Switch Off Fortnight’ and campaigns to reduce food waste. Through these efforts, we empower our pupils to take responsibility for the environment and play an active role in promoting a greener, more sustainable future.
We focus on ten key areas of sustainability, each playing a vital role in achieving our environmental goals. These areas include waste, litter, biodiversity, transport, healthy living, energy, school grounds, global citizenship, water and marine conservation. By teaching our girls about these critical aspects of sustainability, we are making their environmental awareness grow and encouraging them to make a positive difference, both locally and globally.
Sustainability at Maltman’s Green goes beyond just classroom lessons. We encourage hands-on learning experiences, whether through nature-based activities, recycling projects, or gardening initiatives. Each girl learns how her actions can contribute to a healthier planet, and by embedding these lessons into daily school life, we are making their future brighter and more sustainable.
By participating in ‘Walk to School Week’ and other sustainability-focused events, our girls not only improve their own environmental impact but also inspire their families and communities to do the same.
Choosing Maltman’s Green means choosing a school that is dedicated to creating environmentally responsible individuals.

ISI Inspection - Why Choose Maltman's Green Preparatory
pageCache.text:
Thursday 15 May 2025
ISI Inspection – Why Inspectors Were So Impressed by Maltman’s Green Prep
At Maltman’s Green, we talk often about our commitment to girls “Making Their Way”, not as a tagline, but as a living, breathing philosophy that shapes everything we do. It’s our promise to every girl who walks through our doors: that she will be supported, inspired and guided to find her voice and her confidence to make her way in the world.
Our recent March 2025 Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) inspection affirmed that our promise is not just aspirational and that it is being fulfilled. We are delighted to share that the school met all of the required standards across every inspection category, including leadership and governance, the quality of education, pupil development, wellbeing, and safeguarding.
The report is not just a list of benchmarks met — it’s a celebration of who we are and what we stand for.
Leadership that Leads with Purpose
The inspectors recognised the strength and clarity of leadership at all levels of the school, describing it as: “Visible, knowledgeable, reflective and strategic.”
They noted how our ethos, underpinned by our guiding principle that “Better Never Ends”, is not just ambition but embedded in daily routines, decision-making and long-term planning. They observed that our ethos fosters high expectations, reflective practice and a strong focus on pupil wellbeing, inclusion and achievement.
Teaching that Sparks Independence and Curiosity
The report praised the quality of our teaching, noting that it is: “Engaging, fostering pupils’ independence, curiosity and active participation in lessons.”
From our systematic early years programmes to our cross-curricular STEAM projects, inspectors saw a school where girls are excited by learning and empowered to think critically and independently. They observed specialist-led lessons in the creative and physical subjects, and highlighted how these experiences enhance teamwork, resilience and wider skill development.
This validation is particularly meaningful because it affirms what our families already know: that learning at Maltman’s Green is rich, varied and personalised — and always designed with each girl’s growth in mind.
A Culture of Care and Inclusion
Perhaps most significantly, the ISI report highlights the warm, respectful and inclusive culture that lies at the heart of our school. Inspectors wrote:
“Leaders foster an inclusive and supportive environment in which pupils are valued.” “Teachers successfully promote emotional resilience, kindness and self-awareness.” “Staff consistently foster a culture of inclusion and empathy, enabling pupils to appreciate diversity and demonstrate kindness in their interactions.”
These comments go to the core of what it means to be a Maltman’s girl. Our pupils are not only well taught — they are well known, well cared for and given the emotional tools to navigate life with compassion and strength.
From Wellbeing Wednesdays and peer mentoring to kindness cups and pupil voice initiatives, our girls are learning not just how to succeed — but how to support one another, speak up, and lead with empathy.
Preparing Them for the Future
As girls move through the school, they gradually take on more responsibility and develop leadership skills in real and meaningful ways. The inspectors noted:
“Older pupils take on increasing responsibility, developing leadership skills and integrity, preparing them effectively for future stages of education and their role in wider society.”
Whether they’re acting as House Captains, Mindfulness Ambassadors or Prefects, our girls are not just participating in school life — they are helping shape it.
We invite all parents — current and prospective — to read the full ISI report.
It is a source of pride for us as members of the strong team that is Maltman’s, but also a source of reassurance for you as parents of amazing girls.
Ultimately, this report confirms what we’ve always known: that Maltman’s Green is not just preparing girls for the next stage — it’s empowering them to thrive, lead and make their way in the world with confidence, courage and compassion.
